1. F35 — ACCEPT closure of the exact defect

The defect was:

root.revision == anchor.revision + 1

was treated as sufficient evidence that the ahead root was the honest deployment's interrupted successor.

That proved only:

ORDER

not:

PROVENANCE / AUTHORIZATION

A valid successor produced from the same ancestor under a different anchor could occupy the same one-ahead position.

R0.8.6 changes the anchor from:

committed revision/head

to:

committed revision/head
+
pending successor revision/head

and writes the pending authorization before the root records the pending transition.

The admission question is now:

"is this exact next head the one this anchor authorized?"

rather than:

"is this candidate exactly one revision ahead?"

The foreign-successor control is a direct falsifier and flips FAIL -> PASS.

Ruling

F35 exact foreign-successor-substitution defect: CLOSED under:

single host
one protected deployment-owned anchor namespace
trusted root/anchor directory
content-addressed canonical successor head

This is a real strengthening of S3 continuity.

2. The order-of-checks repair is correct

I particularly accept moving anchor reconciliation out of Root::open.

Previously a candidate could move the trust anchor before Ctl::open had verified:

store re-derivation
canonical head
schema contract
integrity_check

R0.8.6 now:

Root::open:
    validates whether an ahead root was authorized
    DOES NOT advance the anchor

Ctl::open:
    validates the candidate store/root semantics
    THEN reconcile_anchor()

That is the correct trust ordering.

A trust anchor must not be advanced merely because an untrusted candidate has the right numerical shape.

3. No F36 is demonstrated — but one new crash cut is not directly witnessed

I do not see evidence in this bundle of a new F36 that re-opens the F35 semantic repair.

However, the repair introduces a new load-bearing sequence:

A. anchor pending-successor authorization persisted
B. root pending transition persisted
C. store successor committed
D. root committed
E. anchor committed / pending authorization cleared

The existing runtime crash hook:

after-pending

fires after Root::set_pending() returns, therefore after both A and B.

It does not directly hit:

A succeeded
B did not happen

nor the sibling case:

A succeeded
root persistence B returned an error

The source ordering is sensible, but this exact cut is now load-bearing because A is new trusted durable state.

Required control before freezing R0.8

Add a small NC29 or equivalent fault-injection control:

NC29 — anchor-authorized / root-unwritten crash cut

1. start from committed R/H0
2. compute intended successor H1
3. persist anchor pending R+1/H1
4. inject process death or root-persist failure BEFORE root pending lands
5. restart against root/store still at R/H0

It should establish explicitly:

a. the controller does not invent that H1 committed;
b. a one-ahead root Hforeign != H1 is refused;
c. the exact H1 successor, if later presented with a semantically matching
   canonical store, is the only ahead successor the anchor can admit;
d. after an explicit replacement/cancellation policy (if replacement is
   permitted before the root pending lands), the old H1 can no longer be
   admitted;
e. the recovery/report surface exposes enough state to distinguish
   "nothing ever authorized" from "successor H1 was durably authorized but
   the root never recorded pending", OR the design explicitly documents why
   that distinction is intentionally not externally observable.

This is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated defect.

Do not mint F36 unless the control actually produces an unsafe or dishonest state.

6. Evidence-state promotion schema — ACCEPT, with four additions

The current promotion record shape is good:

record_id
from
to
sensitivity_witness
executed
executed_by
runtime
pre_fix_witness
repair_witness
promoted_in
history

I would keep it, but I recommend four fields/normalizations before making it a long-term factory contract.

A. use stable class tokens separately from prose

Do not make giant prose strings in from / to the machine comparison.

Prefer:

{
  "from_token": "FALSIFIED",
  "to_token": "TESTED-CONDITIONAL",
  "from_detail": "...",
  "to_detail": "..."
}

The prose remains useful for humans; the token is what the station reasons over.

B. bind the subject implementation

Every executed promotion should carry:

subject_identity:
    repo
    commit
    tree
    artifact digest where applicable

A runtime receipt without the exact subject identity is weaker than it needs to be.

C. bind adjudication when adjudication is required

For cross-lane evidence classes such as this R0.8.6 closure:

adjudication_ref
adjudicator
adjudicated_at

should be available.

Execution and adjudication are distinct acts.

D. make the projection generated, not a second hand-authored registry

evidence_state.json should be a deterministic projection from canonical lane registries + promotion records.

Its own hash should go in the station receipt.

That avoids solving registry drift by creating one more registry to drift.

7. Should every lane be required to provide evidence_state.json?

At promotion/freeze/closure boundaries: YES.

On every ordinary development commit: NO.

Recommended station rule:

if a lane requests any of:
    evidence-class promotion
    FALSIFIED -> repaired/tested
    OPEN -> CLOSED/FROZEN
    candidate -> accepted/corollary
    scope/trust-profile strengthening

then:
    an evidence-state projection is mandatory
    and the generic validator must admit it

If the lane claims no evidence-state transition, the station can instead derive:

promotions = 0

and prove the projection is unchanged.

This keeps the epistemic discipline at the exact place it matters without turning every code edit into registry ceremony.

9. E-51 / E-50a — "unresolved or satisfied" needs one refinement

The model found an important correction:

blocking UNKNOWN only is insufficient

because a same-key replay after an already-COMMITTED intent is also a second effect by construction on a naive far side.

So this statement is correct:

a claim whose stable intent key is unresolved OR already satisfied is not a freely claimable fresh attempt.

But I would not use the same override for both states.

Unresolved intent

For:

UNKNOWN / indeterminate completion

the S5 rule applies:

refuse ordinary replay
OR
require REPLAY_RISK_AUTHORIZED

because the operator is explicitly accepting the possibility that the prior attempt already landed.

Already satisfied intent

For:

COMMITTED
SUPERSEDED because another attempt satisfied the intent

the same intent is already done.

The normal behavior should be:

do not execute another effect under the same intent key
return / derive the existing satisfaction

REPLAY_RISK_AUTHORIZED should not normally turn a satisfied intent into a license to repeat it.

If the user actually wants another physical effect, that is a new intent, even if it is semantically related to the previous one:

new effect_key / intent_id
repeat_of = old_intent
fresh approval / authority

If the product wants a special "knowingly repeat the same satisfied action" operation, give it a different concept such as:

REPEAT_INTENT_AUTHORIZED

rather than overloading uncertainty replay.

Correct E-50a trigger

Therefore:

key has UNKNOWN:
    blocked unless REPLAY_RISK_AUTHORIZED

key is SATISFIED:
    blocked as already satisfied;
    a new physical effect requires a new intent identity

key attempts all FAILED-ABSENT:
    retry/new attempt under same intent is admissible

This is cleaner than one override for both uncertainty and known completion.

10. Strict reconciler on an unkeyed far side — ACCEPT

Yes.

If the far side provides no stable effect identity, a lookup that does not find a keyed record cannot prove:

the effect did not happen

Therefore:

UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN

is the honest reconciliation result.

Progress then requires explicit duplicate-risk authority.

That is exactly S5:

absence of evidence
!=
evidence of non-completion

The strict reconciler is the correct default for an unkeyed/unanalyzable far side.

11. E-50b — ACCEPT the identity split

The model's separation is correct:

INTENT
ATTEMPT
RISK AUTHORIZATION
ATTEMPT TERMINAL
INTENT SATISFACTION

SUPERSEDED is a useful attempt-level terminal relation:

this attempt did not land
another attempt of this intent did

It must not be confused with the intent's outcome itself.

A far-side record should name:

intent/effect key
attempt id
effect id / result

and reconciliation attributes the result to the actual attempt.

This is a good Super/ampd handoff.

12. L1 offer/attach refinement — ACCEPT, but one third system property is implicit

The v2.6 split is a real improvement:

ENV-SUCCESSOR:
    a valid willing successor is offered

SYS-ATTACH-FAIRNESS:
    a continuously enabled valid attach is eventually processed

The finite witness correctly shows neither alone is enough.

However, the model makes attach enabled automatically whenever:

holder == none
and
offered != none

That hides one real-system obligation.

In the actual architecture, an offered successor may still need:

authority
grant / capability
policy permission
generation/finality proof
resource compatibility
world/locus admission

before attach becomes enabled.

So the real contract should distinguish:

ENV-SUCCESSOR-AVAILABILITY
    an eligible/willing candidate exists and is offered

SYS-SUCCESSOR-ENABLEMENT
    after valid finality + a valid offer, the system establishes or recognizes
    the authority/policy state that makes at least one successor attachment
    admissible

SYS-ATTACH-FAIRNESS
    once that admissible attach remains enabled, the scheduler/control plane
    does not postpone it forever

If the phrase "valid offer" is defined to include every system-owned authority precondition, the third item is hidden inside the environment assumption, which is the wrong ownership boundary.

I recommend making SYS-SUCCESSOR-ENABLEMENT explicit in the next temporal model.

It is not necessarily another irreducible L-law; it may be a mechanism obligation required to discharge L1 under the continue-service policy.

13. E-43 A-IDEMPOTENT — useful, with a boundary warning

The measured refinement is sensible:

same scope source digest:
    semantic no-op

changed source digest:
    world transition

But the adapter currently keeps the source digest outside the World.

A native implementation must make:

compare source digest
+
decide no-op/change
+
mutate registry/version/log

one protected semantic operation.

Otherwise the no-op optimization can introduce a TOCTOU hole between the external digest check and the World mutation.

This belongs in the TRVM governance decision.

14. E-42 L-ANCESTRY — useful, but governance still owns fork semantics

The experiment shows why both coordinates matter:

world / birth identity
+
history position / ancestry

A pre-fork warrant can be portable to a descendant if the architecture deliberately says:

fork creates a descendant world identity with explicit ancestry

while twins/copies outside fork() remain unrelated.

That is coherent.

But whether a warrant SHOULD cross a fork remains a semantic policy choice.

The TRVM lane should choose first:

fork = new independent world
or
fork = descendant world with inherited ancestry

Then warrant portability follows from that choice.

The R10-pre lane was right not to promote the law itself.

v4 is another strong execution return.

Most important changes in knowledge:

  1. F35's exact foreign-successor attack is CLOSED.

  2. The anchor now authorizes identity, not merely freshness/order.

  3. Trust-anchor movement occurs only after semantic candidate validation.

already-satisfied repetition should not share one override.
